properties.statement:
ALEX'S EARLIER GROK BUILD SESSION NOTES (~2026-08-07/08, binary 0.24.0, a real monorepo, 361 nodes / 621 edges) TRIAGED AGAINST 0.32.1 — a SECOND file, distinct from the 2026-08-14 report already captured as `art:alex-grok-feedback-2026-08-14`. Confirmed distinct by checksum: the 08-14 artifact is `sha256:0318c290…` and this one is `sha256:007e2868…`. It had never been triaged.

⭐ HIS TOP-PRIORITY ASK DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE. §1.1: `set_decision_status` failing with `Node not found` immediately after a successful `add_decision`, 'especially in a parallel tool batch', which he ranked #1 of six and called 'top pain'. TESTED HERE on 0.32.1 against the shared server, twice: a 2-call batch (create + set status in one message) and a 6-call batch (three creates + three status sets interleaved in one message). ALL EIGHT CALLS SUCCEEDED; every decision came back `proposed` from the create and `accepted` from the set. Scratch nodes deleted afterwards.

⚠️ NOT REPRODUCED IS NOT REFUTED, and three differences could each explain it: he ran 0.24.0 and this is 0.32.1, eight minor versions apart; his harness is Grok Build and this is Claude Code, which may serialise MCP calls within a turn even when they are issued together; and his load was heavier than a six-call batch. ⇒ The honest status is that the reported failure does not occur in THIS configuration, and nobody has yet tested the one where it did.

WHAT IS ALREADY ANSWERED, so it does not need re-asking:
• §2.3 (revising an accepted Requirement by re-calling `add_requirement` erodes intent silently; he asked for a warning) — SHIPPED in v0.32.0 as the constructor `revision` block, which reports the properties overwritten WITH their prior values in full. Exactly his ask, arrived independently from four other reports.
• §4.3 (Capabilities have no `deferred`/`dropped`, so agents write DROPPED into the description) — SETTLED by Anthony as no cancelled state, ever. The ask is declined rather than open.
• §3.1 (large results truncated, `get_instructions` named) — measured during the 08-14 triage and attributed to HIS CLIENT rather than the server.

WHAT SURVIVES AS GENUINELY OPEN, in his own priority order:
① `get_node` BY ID WITHOUT `node_type` (his #3). An agent holds an id from `search_design` and not its type; the lookup then fails. Distinct from the already-fixed 'unknown node_type is refused rather than answered null'.
② SESSION-SCOPED `loop_status` (his #4): 'always dirty on mature graphs — agents ignore or thrash', asking for a 'debt introduced this session' filter. ⭐ CORROBORATED FIRST-HAND AND HARD: across this entire session `loop_status` reported the identical 80 unsurfaced gaps and 16 structural defects from first call to last, and the only way to say anything useful was to compute the delta by hand and report 'unchanged from session start' each time. The per-CONTRIBUTOR scoping that exists is a different axis and does not answer this.
③ IDEMPOTENT LINK HELPERS with a result flag (his #5) — whether re-calling `satisfies`/`allocate`/`contains` is a no-op or an error is undocumented.
④ A HARNESS-AGNOSTIC SESSION-END NUDGE (his #6): on Grok Build `loop_status` reports `nudge: absent` and there is no alternative, so under load agents capture and skip detect-and-ask. He suggests a `session_wrap_up` tool an agent can call. Note this is the SAME failure the loop nudge exists to prevent, arriving on the harness that cannot host it.
⑤ OPTIONAL `status` ON `add_decision` (his #2) — and this is CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY by dev_storyflow's dragon Boss the same week ('there is no one-call path to an accepted decision', six times in one session). ⚠️ BUT BOTH RUN INTO ACCEPTED DOCTRINE: `add_decision` deliberately stopped defaulting to `accepted` on 2026-07-25, and `dec:certainty-derived` holds that moving a status is the owner's word. Alex concedes the point himself — 'default proposed is correct for honesty' — and asks only for an optional override. That makes this a question for Anthony rather than a defect.

HIS FRAMING TO KEEP, and it is a priority instruction rather than a finding: 'DO NOT spend meaningful engineering effort on one-time migration' from the early-adopter era (dropping old skill folders, untracking RocksDB layout, rewriting long AGENTS.md). 'Most users will never have to do that upgrade.' Invest instead in keeping future upgrades boring — install.sh replacing binary and kit while never touching graphs, which he names as already the right model.
